items.stem: Why does holding assets with low correlation reduce portfolio risk?

options.text: Their returns do not move together, so swings partly offset
options.rationale: Correct: imperfect correlation dampens overall volatility.
They can still fall; correlation is about co-movement, not safety.
Diversification targets risk, not guaranteed higher return.
Systematic market risk cannot be diversified away.

items.explanation: Correct: imperfect correlation dampens overall volatility.

items.stem: An investor compares two equity funds tracking the same index. Which TWO factors most justify choosing the cheaper one? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: lower recurring fees compound to a large difference over time.

options.text: Lower tracking difference to the index
options.rationale: Correct: closer tracking means the fund delivers the index return more faithfully.
Past return does not predict future results and may reflect noise.
Brand does not improve net returns for an index fund.

items.explanation: Correct: fees and tracking are the durable differentiators for index funds.

items.stem: An investor with a 20-year horizon panics during a market fall and sells to cash. What is the main risk of this action?

options.text: Locking in losses and missing the recovery
options.rationale: Correct: selling low realises the loss and risks missing rebounds.
Fee level is not the main issue; realised loss is.
Moving to cash reduces, not increases, diversification.
Abandoning the plan typically lowers long-run outcomes.
